title: Record of processing activities
subtitle: Okiru as operator for Super Group — POPIA section 21 register
stamp: Okiru ESG Intelligence Platform · Record of processing activities · Super Group · v1.0 · 17 September 2026 · Commercial in confidence
intro: This register records what personal information Okiru processes on Super Group's instruction, why, where it goes, how long it is kept and who can reach it. It is the per-client record that section 17 of POPIA expects a responsible party to be able to produce, prepared from the operator's side so that Super Group does not have to reconstruct it.

Super Group is the responsible party for the information listed here. Okiru is the operator, processing only on Super Group's documented instruction. Nothing in this register creates a purpose of our own.

verification.label: Scope of this register
verification.body: ESG and B-BBEE reporting for Super Group and its operating units. It covers personal information only — the great majority of what we process for Super Group is operational measurement (litres, kilowatt-hours, tonnes) that is not personal information at all, and is not listed here.

blocks.label: Special personal information
blocks.text: Race is special personal information under section 26 of POPIA, and B-BBEE scoring cannot be produced without it. Section 27(1)(b) permits processing where it is required by law, and the B-BBEE Act and the Codes of Good Practice are that law. We process it as aggregated counts by designated group, never as individual records, and it is never used for any purpose other than producing the scorecard. Health information arising from safety incidents is limited to counts; we neither request nor want the underlying medical detail.

blocks.text: Every access to client data by an Okiru person is recorded in the audit trail, which Super Group can retrieve for itself at any time as CSV or JSON. The trail is signed per record and sealed daily, so it can be checked for tampering rather than taken on trust.

blocks.label: Why erasure does not delete the audit trail
blocks.text: Erasing a person removes everything that identifies them, and keeps the audit records of what their account did with the actor reduced to an opaque identifier. Deleting those records instead would erase the evidence of processing that the accountability condition exists to preserve — a client could no longer prove who touched their data. The person is no longer identifiable from the trail; the processing history survives.

items: Encryption at rest under a customer-managed key we hold and can revoke; TLS 1.2 or better in transit.
Two-factor authentication required for every account that can reach client data.
A web application firewall and rate limiting in front of every public endpoint.
An audit trail that is signed per record, sealed daily, and copied to storage under a 730-day immutability policy.
Nightly backups held twice, with a restore rehearsed and verified quarterly rather than assumed.
A written incident-response plan committing to notify the client within 24 hours of a confirmed or likely exposure.

blocks.text: The full position, including what is not yet in place, is in the accompanying security and POPIA disclosure. This register is deliberately not the place to summarise gaps: that document lists them with a risk and a remediation, and the two should be read together.
